title: Idle-pocket mapping: CUDA Graph photography and kernel-gap timeline notes
content:
Purpose:
Short notes from an exploratory profiling session focused on small "idle pockets" that appear between CUDA-graph-captured kernel groups. The aim is to understand whether these gaps are: (a) real SM idle time caused by prefetch/async-copy alignment or stream handoff, (b) host-side serialization during graph replay, or (c) an artifact of our capture / NVTX annotation.

Quick summary / TL;DR:
- Observed recurring 60-240us gaps between logically adjacent kernels inside a single cudaGraph replay. Gaps coincide with a drop in SM active % and a transient increase in L2 miss-rate for the following kernel.
- Gaps appear less frequently when using single-stream capture + tight kernel fusion; they are more frequent with graph fragments created by our current capture heuristic (we capture per-layer group).
- Primary hypothesis: prefetch window mismatch + device-side stream priority preemption combined with small async-copy staging causes SM wake latency. Secondary hypothesis: kernel launches that cross page boundaries (host pinned buffer alignment) can introduce micro-synchronization at the driver level.

Hardware / stack:
- HW: NVIDIA A100-SXM4 (80GB) in cloud smoke org (dev-cluster-03) and a 2xH100 test node for confirmation.
- Driver: 525.89.02 (A100 runs)
- cuda: 12.2
- Runtime: redwood-inference-serving-runtime v1.14.3 (local dev build)
- Capture tools: Nsight Systems 2026.4, Nsight Compute 2026.3 (lightweight sampling + timeline), nvprof->nsight timeline conversion used for some older traces.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Build a small reproduction harness that replays a typical decode loop (microbatch=4, seq_out=256, kv-prefetch enabled): ./bin/graph_replay_test --model small-decoder --microbatch 4 --seq 256 --prefetch on --iters 120
2) Capture with: nsys profile --output idle-pocket-101226 --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=cpu --duration-mode=timeline --capture-range=cpu -- ./bin/graph_replay_test ...
3) Open in Nsight and focus on the timeline slice where latency spikes (~iteration 38-42). Add SM activity and CUDA kernel occupancy panels. Export CSV for kernel start/end timestamps for the suspicious window.

Key observations (timestamped from trace idle-pocket-101226):
- 00:01:12.422: Kernel A (matmul-0) ends at T0. SM active drops from ~92% to ~12% over 20us.
- 00:01:12.509: Kernel B (softmax-1) starts at T0 + 87us. Between there, we see a short asyncMemcpy D2H (staging buffer) start/end (~5us) and a small host-side API call (cuGraphInstantiate / cuGraphLaunch wrapper) that takes ~30us.
- NVTX shows enter/exit annotations for graph-segment boundaries aligned with our layer-grouping. The host-side cuGraphLaunch wrapper frequently performs a small write to a device-side signaling buffer (writes 8 bytes). Those writes are serialized with CUDA stream operations and appear in the timeline immediately before the gap.
- L2 read-latency and L2-miss-rate for Kernel B are elevated for the initial 10% of its execution (consistent with cold cache after an idle).

Micro-metrics from Nsight Compute samples (30us sampling, combined across 20 runs):
- Average inter-kernel gap inside graph replay: 102us (stdev 48us)
- Median warp_efficiency for kernels starting after gap: 86% vs 94% normally
- SM_active duty-cycle at gap trough: 8% (baseline between kernels steady-state ~87%)
- SMMU page fault events: none in traces captured (ruling out page faults here)

Interpretation / possible root causes:
1) Small host-side serialization in our cuGraph wrapper (the 30us host CPU region) can delay signaling. Although cuGraphLaunch is async, our wrapper performs an extra synchronous write to a device control word which ends up serialized with the stream. That write + host scheduling jitter explains the ~30us slice. Remaining gap (~70us) looks like device-side wake time (SM wake + prefetch).
2) Device prefetching: we use an eager KV prefetch stage that triggers an async copy into a device scratch before compute kernels. If that prefetch completes slightly earlier than kernel dispatch, the device may be in a low-power SM idle with cache invalidation happening. When the kernel starts, L2 misses spike while the data warms up. The prefetches are on different streams and can be deprioritized by stream priority preemption.
3) Kernel small-fusion artifact: our capture heuristic breaks the graph into many small nodes to keep graphs re-usable. Each small node leads to a micro-scheduling gap in the hardware scheduler, particularly when combined with stream priority / default stream interplay.

Quick experiments run (results):
- Turned off the device-side 8-byte signaling write: gaps reduced by ~28% (median gap -> 73us) but not eliminated.
- Collapsed two adjacent captured nodes into a fused kernel using our JIT fusion harness: gaps reduced to <20us and L2 cold miss transient significantly reduced.
- Set prefetch stream to higher priority: gaps reduced by ~40% in average cases; worst-case (when host CPU is contended) still shows ~40us residual.
- Tried cuGraphLaunch with cudaStreamWaitEvent vs explicit signaling elimination: behavior similar; suggests some of the cost is at kernel dispatch + SM wake rather than purely host synchrony.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Is there driver-side queue consolidation that triggers when small host writes to device control buffers occur? (ask drivers/infra team for traces at driver level)
- Does this scale linearly with microbatch size? (we saw smaller gaps at higher microbatch, propose a small sweep)
- Is there a measurable difference on H100 (tensor core warm-up characteristics different)? Quick H100 runs show reduced gaps (~30-50% less) but dataset limited.

Suggested mitigations (short-term to test in prod branch):
- Avoid the 8-byte signaling write; switch to using events with cudaStreamWaitEvent on an internal high-priority stream where possible.
- Increase fusion aggressiveness for layer-groups that are < 0.5ms to reduce number of replay nodes.
- Move prefetches to a high-priority stream and ensure prefetch -> compute handoff uses an event recorded on the high-priority stream so compute isn't starved behind lower-priority host activities.
- Introduce a tiny no-op kernel (warm-up) immediately before the first compute kernel in a fragment to reduce L2 cold miss transient (measured warm-up reduced L2 miss spike by ~70% in a short test). This is hacky but lower-risk to test quickly.

Notes for next runs / checklist:
- Capture: enable "API tracing" + timeline + kernel occupancy view. Export kernel start/end CSV and overlay with NVTX markers. Save nsight project to gs://redwood-profiles/idle-pocket-2026-10/ for audits.
- Run wide sweep: microbatch {1,2,4,8}, seq_out {128,256,512}, prefetch: {on,off,high-priority}. Collect 10 traces each and aggregate inter-kernel gap stats.
- Add a tiny instrumentation to our cuGraph wrapper to record timestamps for: before-write-to-control-word, after-write, after-cuGraphLaunch-call return to better separate host vs device timing.

Action items (owners):
- Asha: push a bench branch that disables signaling write + adds high-priority prefetch option (due 2026-10-20).
- Luca: prepare fusion-run sweep harness and attempt automated fusion for small nodes (due 2026-10-25).
- Priya: schedule a brief sync with driver team to share trace and ask about driver-level consolidation/serialization (target 2026-10-18).

Appendix (quick commands & links):
- NSYS capture: nsys profile --output idle-pocket-101226 --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=cpu -- ./bin/graph_replay_test --args
- NVTX helper used: decorators in runtime/common/nvtx_utils.h (search for "GRAPH_SEG_BOUNDARY")
- Quick CSV extraction script: tools/trace_tools/extract_kernel_windows.py --nsys idle-pocket-101226.qdrep --out idle-pocket-101226.csv
- Trace stored: gs://redwood-profiles/idle-pocket-2026-10/idle-pocket-101226.qdrep

Rough timeline expectation:
- If mitigations look promising in bench branch, ship prefetch->high-priority and signaling-write removal to canary in dedicated cluster for 2 weeks and track inter-kernel-gap metric in Console (per-route instrumentation).

Notes to future reader:
This doc is intentionally exploratory and contains raw observations. It is likely some of the artifacts are noise from our capture setup; follow the checklist and centralize traces in the gs:// path above. If any of the team wants me to run a tailored capture on dedicated infra (H100 backed), ping me and I will schedule longer runs.

Unresolved: link the driver-side trace and confirm whether the driver consolidates small host writes into a serialized work item — that will change the mitigation direction (driver-level vs runtime-level).

-- Asha
